    input [1:0] divisor,
    output reg [1:0] quotient,
    output reg [1:0] remainder
);

description: Design a watchdog timer that resets itself if it receives a "kick" signal within a specified timeout period. The timer will have a clock input, a reset input, a kick input, and an output indicating whether the timer has timed out. If the kick signal is received before the timeout period, the timer should reset. If the timeout period elapses without receiving a kick, the timer output should indicate a timeout condition.
code:
module watchdog_timer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire kick,
    output reg timeout
);
    parameter TIMEOUT_PERIOD = 8'd100; // Set timeout period
    reg [7:0] counter;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            counter <= 8'd0;
            timeout <= 1'b0;
        end else if (kick) begin
            counter <= 8'd0; // Reset counter on kick
            timeout <= 1'b0;
        end else begin
            if (counter < TIMEOUT_PERIOD) begin
                counter <= counter + 1;
            end else begin
                timeout <= 1'b1; // Set timeout flag
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 32-bit serializer that converts a 32-bit parallel input into a serial output bitstream. The serializer should shift out one bit on each clock cycle. The input data should be loaded when a 'load' signal is asserted, and the serial output should be available on each clock cycle when the 'load' signal is high. Once the entire 32 bits have been transmitted, the serializer should stop until a new load signal is received.
code:
module serializer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire load,
    input wire [31:0] data_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [5:0] bit_count; // To count the bits shifted out
    reg [31:0] shift_reg; // Shift register to hold the input data

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (load) begin
            // Load data into the shift register and reset the bit counter
            shift_reg <= data_in;
            bit_count <= 0;
        end else if (bit_count < 32) begin
            // Shift out one bit
            serial_out <= shift_reg[31]; // Get the MSB
            shift_reg <= shift_reg << 1; // Shift left
            bit_count <= bit_count + 1; // Increment the bit counter
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a Bluetooth communication controller that manages the state of a Bluetooth device. The device can be in one of three states: IDLE, CONNECTING, and CONNECTED. The controller has input signals to initiate the connection and to disconnect. The state transitions are as follows: 
1. From IDLE to CONNECTING when the `start_connection` signal is high. 
2. From CONNECTING to CONNECTED when the `connection_done` signal is high. 
3. From CONNECTED to IDLE when the `disconnect` signal is high. 
4. The state remains the same if none of the signals are triggered.
code:
module bluetooth_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input start_connection,
    input connection_done,
    input disconnect,
    output reg [1:0] state // 00: IDLE, 01: CONNECTING, 10: CONNECTED
);

    // State encoding
    parameter IDLE = 2'b00;
    parameter CONNECTING = 2'b01;
    parameter CONNECTED = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start_connection) begin
                        state <= CONNECTING;
                    end
                end
                CONNECTING: begin
                    if (connection_done) begin
                        state <= CONNECTED;
                    end
                end
                CONNECTED: begin
                    if (disconnect) begin
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input [3:0] data_in,
    input clk,
    input rst,
    output reg [2:0] crc_out
);
    reg [6:0] shift_reg;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            shift_reg <= 7'b0;
            crc_out <= 3'b0;
        end else begin
            shift_reg <= {shift_reg[5:0], data_in}; // Shift in data

                shift_reg[6:3] = shift_reg[6:3] ^ 4'b1011; // x^3 + x + 1
            end
            crc_out <= shift_reg[2:0]; // Output last 3 bits as CRC

    end
endmodule

    output reg vco_out             // VCO output
);

    reg [15:0] div_counter;          // Divider counter
    reg [15:0] vco_freq;             // VCO frequency

            div_counter <= 0;
            vco_freq <= 0;

                div_counter <= div_counter + 1;
            end

                vco_out <= ~vco_out; // Toggle VCO output

            end
        end
    end
endmodule

module crc_generator(

    input reset,
    input [15:0] data_in,
    input [15:0] polynomial,
    output reg [15:0] crc_out
);
    reg [15:0] crc_reg;
    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            crc_reg <= 16'h0000;
            crc_out <= 16'h0000;
        end else begin
            crc_reg <= data_in; // Initialize CRC with data input
            for (i = 0; i < 16; i = i + 1) begin
                if (crc_reg[15] == 1'b1) begin
                    crc_reg = (crc_reg << 1) ^ polynomial; // Shift and XOR with polynomial
                end else begin
                    crc_reg = crc_reg << 1; // Just shift
                end
            end
            crc_out <= crc_reg; // Output the final CRC value
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Direct Memory Access (DMA) controller in Verilog that can read data from a source address and write it to a destination address in memory. The controller should handle a finite number of transactions defined by a transfer count. Input signals include a clock, reset, start signal, source address, destination address, and transfer count. The output signals should indicate the status of the DMA transfer (busy, done) and the data being transferred.
code:
module dma_controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] source_addr,
    input wire [7:0] dest_addr,
    input wire [3:0] transfer_count,
    output reg busy,
    output reg done,
    output reg [7:0] data_out
);
    reg [3:0] count;
    reg [7:0] memory [0:255]; // Example memory for DMA

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            busy <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            count <= 0;
        end else if (start && !busy) begin
            busy <= 1;
            count <= transfer_count;
            data_out <= memory[source_addr]; // Read data from source address
        end else if (busy) begin
            if (count > 0) begin
                memory[dest_addr] <= data_out; // Write data to destination address
                count <= count - 1;
                data_out <= memory[source_addr + (transfer_count - count)]; // Load next data
            end else begin
                busy <= 0;
                done <= 1; // Signal that the operation is complete
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

If no error is detected, the system will proceed to the next data word.

module ARQ (

    input rst,
    input [4:0] data_in,
    input error_detected,
    output reg [4:0] data_out,
    output reg ack
);

        if (rst) begin
            data_out <= 5'b00000;
            last_valid_data <= 5'b00000;
            ack <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (error_detected) begin
                data_out <= last_valid_data; // resend last valid data
                ack <= 0; // no acknowledgment since there was an error
            end else begin

Design a LIFO stack in Verilog with the following specifications:
1. The stack should have a maximum size of 8 elements.
2. Inputs:
   - `push`: a signal to push data onto the stack (active high).
   - `pop`: a signal to pop data from the stack (active high).
   - `data_in`: an 8-bit input data for pushing onto the stack.
3. Outputs:
   - `data_out`: an 8-bit output data that indicates the value popped from the stack.
   - `empty`: a flag indicating if the stack is empty.
   - `full`: a flag indicating if the stack is full.
code:
module stack (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire push,
    input wire pop,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg empty,
    output reg full
);
    reg [7:0] stack_mem [7:0]; // stack memory of 8 elements
    reg [2:0] top; // to track the top of the stack

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            top <= 3'b000; // reset top
            empty <= 1'b1; // stack is empty
            full <= 1'b0; // stack is not full
            data_out <= 8'b0; // output data
        end else begin
            if (push && !full) begin
                stack_mem[top] <= data_in; // push data
                top <= top + 1;
                if (top == 3'b111) full <= 1'b1; // stack full
                empty <= 1'b0; // stack not empty
            end
            if (pop && !empty) begin
                top <= top - 1;
                data_out <= stack_mem[top]; // pop data
                if (top == 3'b000) empty <= 1'b1; // stack empty
                full <= 1'b0; // stack not full
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

);

);
